sources.title: Niuafoʻou
sources.excerpt: Niuafoʻou is the northernmost island in the kingdom of Tonga. One of the Niua Islands, it is located in the southern Pacific Ocean between Fiji and Samoa, 574 km (357 mi) north of Tongatapu island group and 337 km (209 mi) northwest of Vavaʻu. It is a volcanic rim island with an area of 15 km2 (5.8 sq mi) and a population of 431. The volcano is active and has erupted regularly since 1814, with its last major eruption in 1985.

The Niuas in Tonga
You know you've been everywhere when you have reached The Niuas. The far-flung islands of Niuatoputapu, Niuafo'ou and Tafahi are where time stands still; where locals live the traditional island life and much of the islands are undeveloped. Plan your once-in-a-lifetime trip to The Niuas, right here, on Tonga's largest travel guide.

[[Image:Niuafoʻou.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Niuafo'ou Island from space]]
*'''Niuafo'ou''' is the northernmost island of Tonga. Other names for the island are Good Hope island and Tin Can island. The latter originated from the fact that in earlier times mail was delivered and picked up by strong swimmers who would retrieve packages sealed up in a biscuit tin and thrown overboard from passing ships. Stamps from that time have become a collector's item. It is the tip of an underwater volcano created by sub-oceanic eruptions.
